title: The starter Button comes as Primary, Secondary or Ghost, in three sizes, with an icon
goal: The Button on the Library shelf is one blue button with a label. Ship it the way the variants mock draws it: Primary, Secondary and Ghost looks in Small, Medium and Large, with a leading icon that an instance can show or hide and swap for another, so dropping a Button gives somebody a real, configurable button straight away.
notes: Prerequisite for an-instance-s-properties-match-the-variants-mock (acceptance 3). Depends on the two-variant-property model task. Starter shapes: Sources/PhotonzCore/StarterComponents.swift (StarterComponent.button, button(pen), layout). Properties a copy can set: ComponentProperty kinds .visible (Show icon, already a switch on the instance: InstanceShowKnob), .text (Label), .variant (a piece swap among the original's children: the Icon dropdown). Mock specimens: docs/design/mocks/pages/ui-variants.html .pmatrix cells (btn primary/secondary/ghost x sm/md/lg with ic-sparkle) and its Icon menu (Sparkle, Wand, Swatch, Layers, Brush, No icon). Existing documents that already hold a starter Button keep theirs.
acceptance: A Button dropped from the Library at Next defaults offers Variant (Primary, Secondary, Ghost) and Size (Small, Medium, Large) in its Properties
Picking Secondary or Large changes the instance on the canvas at once, in one undo step each
The instance has a Show icon switch that hides and shows its leading icon, and an Icon dropdown that swaps it, in one undo step each
Each of the nine looks matches its cell in the ui-variants.html matrix in colour, height and padding, in light and dark
On the picked instance, the Show icon switch carries its On or Off word beside it and the Label field is the mock's full-width box with the T glyph in front, as ui-variants.html draws them

log.note: Added from an-instance-s-properties-match-the-variants-mock (2026-10-09): the mock's Show icon switch says On beside it and its Label field is a full-width input with a T glyph; the app's text knob is a narrower rounded field with no glyph. Fold that into this task since it is the Button instance's knobs.

Review before building: a first-time user drops Button and gets a finished control with the knobs the mock lists. What the mock assumed the app lacked: (1) a default look that is not the grid's first (the grid runs Small to Large, the mock's instance is Medium) -> componentDefaultVersion for starters; (2) a choice answer made on one look meant nothing on another look (each look has its own Icon pieces) -> answers map by name across looks; (3) the mock's No icon has no home in a choice knob -> it is the paired Show icon switch's Off, one fact; (4) icons as data -> IconPathData reads icons.mjs path data verbatim. A Figma user expects the button set's default variant and swap; a widened button must keep icon+word centred, so the row is nested inside a free capsule (stacks have no main-axis centring).

Built: PhotonzCore IconPathData (SVG path parser incl. arcs), StarterIcon (5 glyphs), StarterComponents.looks/button(variant,size) (9 drawings, Variant+Size answers, knobs Show icon/Label/Icon shared across looks), componentDefaultVersion, componentChoiceShape (choice answers across looks), piece lookups per copy's look (sourceOfPiece, wordingEdit). Accent #4C6FFF, Muted #5C6371. Panel: Show icon On/Off word, Label well with T glyph, Icon menu with template pictures and No icon. Tests: StarterButtonLooksTests (19) + updated starter/group/placement/library/first-drop tests; full suite 11963 green.

Walks: new starter-button-looks-walk (12 real captures, Next defaults, pointer presses, Icon menu clicked at its face). Updated 16 walks that used the starter Button as a one-look component (moved to Badge/Text Field, or reading the nine looks); all 69 component walks green.

Follow-ups: the-starter-button-primary-shines-like-the-mock (p1: gloss, Icon face glyph, Secondary glass), decide-whether-starter-components-change-colour (decision card on dark mode, acceptance 4's 'and dark'), folded the crowded/illegible Edit Original grid into edit-original-draws-a-two-question-component-ins and raised it to p1.
